description:
From the fz-k22.13 audit, carried forward with corrected names.

`OrderedSet::remove` (src/compiler2/ordered_set.rs) does `members.remove` (O(1))
plus `order.retain` (O(n) over the whole list), and it is called from
`replace_reads` / `replace_waits` on EVERY job re-run, once per
previously-subscribed fact. A fact with large subscriber fan-out could hit
O(n^2).

## What changed since filing

The ticket named `JobSet` in deps.rs; that type no longer exists. fz-f98.19
generalized it into `OrderedSet<T>` in its own module and widened its use: it now
backs the fact subscribers/waiters (as JobSet did) AND `DependencyIndex::outputs`
and `FactReplace::output_keys`, because a job's fact emission order turned out to
be load-bearing for reproducibility.

So the same `remove` is now on more paths than when this was filed, and the
concern is broader rather than narrower. The measurement, however, is still
absent -- nobody has profiled it hot.

## Not urgent, and deliberately so

No measurable delta on current fixtures at filing time (quicksort 0.022s vs
0.026s). This is a watch item: profile before large-fanout workloads, not a
change to make speculatively.

Options if it ever profiles hot: index-assisted swap-remove, or tombstone +
compact. Note that swap-remove would DESTROY insertion order, which is now
load-bearing -- see fz-f98.19 -- so it is no longer an option here without an
explicit order-preserving variant.

## Minimum acceptable outcome

A comment in ordered_set.rs acknowledging the tradeoff against `Agenda`, which
uses a VecDeque and never needs retain because pop_front is its only removal.
The two are not the same idiom; the resemblance is directional, not literal, and
the current module doc does not say so.

## Checks

- Either a profile showing `OrderedSet::remove` is not hot on a large-fanout
  workload, or a fix that preserves insertion order.
- ordered_set.rs documents the retain cost and why Agenda escapes it.
title: OrderedSet::remove is an O(n) retain on the hottest fixpoint paths (was JobSet, now wider)
